what: Recoil numbers for the hold and skin work (research, 2026-10-22). Nothing built from these yet.
owner_asked: find me the force of recoil based on bullet, then tell me the equation to calculate the recoil force back to hand and shoulder, then calculate the recoil force feedback direct to main hand and support hand for pistol (two hands at one place) and for long gun (2 hands at 2 places)

equations.impulse: I = m_b*v + m_c*f*v  (SAAMI Gun Recoil - Technical, Rev. 7/9/2018; gas weight = powder charge; f = 1.50 pistols, 1.75 high powered rifles)
equations.force_to_body: F_avg = I / dt (dt = time the hand or shoulder takes to stop the gun); half-sine pulse peak = (pi/2) * F_avg
equations.muzzle_rise: tau = F * h (h = bore axis height above the contact that takes the push); angular impulse = I * h
equations.friction_hold: a hand that holds only by squeeze can take at most mu * (sum of its normal forces); mu = 0.30 skin on handle (Wu et al. 2014, 2017)

hand_arm_impedance_along_forearm.source: ISO 10068 values as reproduced in ISO 13753:1998 Annex A, Table A.1 (iTeh preview)
hand_arm_impedance_along_forearm.conditions: male hand-arm, along the forearm (zh), ISO posture, 25-50 N grip
hand_arm_impedance_along_forearm.reading: in the recoil band (about 25-500 Hz) the hand-arm acts mostly as a damper of 160-270 N*s/m (phase -6 to +23 deg)

wrist_stiffness.source: The passive stiffness of the wrist and forearm (10 subjects; ResearchGate abstract)
wrist_stiffness.grip_effect: +36% wrist stiffness from no grip to 10% grip (PubMed 25373932)

arm_endpoint_stiffness_slow.source: Endpoint stiffness magnitude increases linearly with a stronger power grasp, Sci Rep 2020, PMC6962455
arm_endpoint_stiffness_slow.note: slow, planar; for the later arm swing, not the 10 ms pulse

segment_mass_percent_body.source: Plagenhoef, Evans and Abdelnour 1983 (male), as tabled by exrx / Frontiers supplement; de Leva 1996 not confirmed

straight_arm.Zhang 2021 Shock and Vibration doi:10.11: 7 men, 10-1000 Hz; below 40 Hz the 180 deg elbow gives higher impedance, 40-100 Hz the 90 deg elbow higher, above 100 Hz posture has no clear effect; more grip or push raises impedance (30-200 Hz) and the peak frequency
straight_arm.Aldien et al. 2005 Industrial Health 43:: 90 vs 180 deg elbow: posture nearly negligible on impedance magnitude; with the arm straight, more grip or push raises absorbed energy a lot; peaks near 25 and 150 Hz
straight_arm.Adewusi et al. (cited): absorbed power 1.63 W straight arm vs 0.67 W bent, same hand forces
straight_arm.Adewusi, Rakheja, Marcotte 2012 Int J In: bent-arm and straight-arm models with fitted masses, springs, dampers: the numbers we need
straight_arm.reading: in the recoil band (about 25-150 Hz) a straight arm changes the impedance little; it matters below 40 Hz (the slower push after the pulse and the muzzle return)

zhang2021_fig8.source: Zhang W et al. Shock and Vibration 2021, 9967278 (owner's PDF), Figure 8, read off the plot; 7 Chinese men (avg 59 kg), zh axis, 30 N grip, 30 N push, 5 m/s2
zhang2021_fig8.method: one-frequency estimate: the pulse's frequency f = (arms*Z)/(2*pi*M) and Z read at f, solved together; a time model fitted to the curve is the next step

arm_chain.adewusi_2010_abstract: owner's PDFs achv-27944-adewusi and Biodynamic_Model...: the same 2-page ACHV 2010 abstract; bent arm only; no parameter values

time_model.owner_said: yes build the time model and show numbers
time_model.model: 3-mass chain fitted to Zhang 2021 Fig. 8 straight arm (|Z| only, 10-500 Hz); gun 1.253 kg on the contact mass; shot = half-sine 3.762 N*s over 1.045 ms (barrel 5 1/32 in, 802 ft/s, even speed-up); two hands = every arm value doubled
time_model.anatomical_masses_tried: masses fixed to Plagenhoef 1983 at 59 kg: fit off by up to 2.7x (rms log 1.0); rejected: the handle meets about 0.05 kg of flesh, not the whole hand
time_model.barrel_time_check: 0.5 / 1.05 / 2.0 ms: two-hand peak per hand 639 / 459 / 436 N; travel and stop time unchanged
time_model.not_modelled: the slide: the gun is taken as one rigid body; the real M1911 frame gets the push through the recoil spring and the slide's hit at full travel

slide_model.owner_said: yes add the slide and show numbers

inputs.slide_kg: 0.380 = 485 g slide+barrel+spring (1911Forum weighing of a Colt Series 70; weak) - barrel 98 g - spring 6.8 g; matches '13 oz bare slide' (370 g, same forum); our model's volume x 7.85 g/cm3 gives 420 g (run as a check)
inputs.recoil_spring: 5013200: 8.00 lb at 3.72 in, 13.55 lb at 1.81 in, 2.88 lb/in, wire .043, OD .430, 30 coils (Ordnance drawing, complete set p.15)
inputs.mainspring: 5013208: 22.0 lb at 1.312 in, 29.5 lb at 1.062 in (same set p.30); cocking work 0.727 J spread over the slide's travel
inputs.barrel_stop: 1/4 in (rangehot.com write-up; weak); 0.10 in run as a check
inputs.travel: 4.755 cm (our model) vs 1.91 in = 4.85 cm from the spring drawing's two lengths
inputs.steel_stops: K_c 1e7-1e9 N/m, damping ratio 0.02-0.5: no source, run as checks

slide_model.not_modelled: cartridge feeding and barrel re-locking on the way forward, friction, the hammer's real stroke; the slide bounces at battery in the model (elastic stops): the closing phase is the weakest part

final_model.cycle_source: 1911Forum 'slide speed analysis' (thread 477846; read from search snippets, page behind a paid bot gateway): optical encoder on a Springfield 1911, 230 gr PMC Bronze FMJ, 2.5 shots, informal: peak slide speed about 25 ft/s, about 10 ms from slide start to frame hit, cycle about 60 ms. Other forum posts: 60-90 ms.

matched.peak_slide_speed: model 7.76 m/s = 25.5 ft/s (no fitting: from the shot's push and the masses)

fitted.what: one lumped drag on the slide's way forward (rails, riding over the cocked hammer and disconnector, extractor over the rim, round up the ramp): no source for each, so fitted to the 60 ms cycle
fitted.sensitivity: 15 N -> 54 ms, 20 N -> 68 ms; any bounce setting zeta 0.5-4 settles the same
